summary: Analog Match is a transparent tool that scores and ranks Earth sites as analogs for a lunar south pole base and for Mars. On the basis of temperature, illumination, terrain, isolation and access, five sites are scored from 1 to 5, with every score tied to a recorded fact and source. Devon Island ranks best for both targets, and Atacama is a close second for Mars. A sensitivity analysis and an interactive map show how rankings change with mission priorities.
details:
What it does: Analog Match scores and ranks Earth sites as analogs for a Moon south pole base and for Mars. Five sites (Devon Island, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Svalbard, Mauna Kea, Atacama Desert) are scored 1 to 5 on temperature, illumination, terrain/regolith, isolation and access, separately for each target. Every one of the 50 scores has a recorded fact, source and scoring rule in an open evidence table (evidence.csv). A sensitivity analysis re-ranks the sites under four priority sets (baseline, power-focused, logistics-first, equal weights), and an interactive map shows the results: https://vect-hunting-git.github.io/analog-match/analog_map.html

Benefits and impact: Mission teams can see which Earth site best fits a given need, such as habitat testing, rover trials or crew training, and why. The method is transparent, so planners can change the weights or add sites.

Results: Moon south pole: Devon Island 4.00, Dry Valleys 3.50, Svalbard 3.25. Mars: Devon Island 3.70, Atacama 3.65, Mauna Kea 3.25. Devon Island is best for both targets (average 3.85). Under a power-focused weighting, Atacama overtakes Devon Island for Mars.

Tools: Python (pandas, matplotlib, folium), VS Code, Google Sheets and Slides, GitHub and GitHub Pages. Reference values for the Moon and Mars come from NASA’s Planetary Fact Sheet.

Creativity and factors considered: We scored the same sites against two targets, so the output shows specialization (polar sites suit the Moon, Atacama and Mauna Kea lean toward Mars) and a best site for both. We kept every score traceable and marked weak evidence as “limited data”.

Limitations and next steps: Scores are judgment-based from public sources. The Moon temperature target is a global mean, not a south pole value. Next steps are LRO Diviner polar data, NASA Earthdata and Worldview imagery, new candidate sites (caves, volcanic and permafrost analogs) and expert validation.
